In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? That is the one who repulses the orphan, and does not urge the feeding of the needy. So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who make show of their deeds, and withhold small kindnesses.﴾

The first: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ That is, denies the requital and the reckoning in the Hereafter, and this has already been discussed in al-Fatihah. The word "ara'ayta" is written with the second hamzah retained, since one does not say "ray'ta" in "ara'ayta," but the hamzah of interrogation made the hamzah an alif; this was mentioned by al-Zajjaj. In the sentence there is an ellipsis, and the meaning is: "Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense: is he right or is he wrong?"

Scholars differed about who this was revealed concerning. Abu Salih related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: it was revealed concerning al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi; this was also said by al-Kalbi and Muqatil. Al-Dahhak related from him that he said: it was revealed concerning a man among the hypocrites. Al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. It was also said concerning Abu Jahl. Al-Dahhak said: concerning ʿAmr ibn ʿAʾidh. Ibn Jurayj said: it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan, who used to slaughter a camel every week; an orphan asked him for something, so he struck him with his staff, and Allah revealed this surah.

"Yadu''u" means "pushes away," as He said: ﴿They are pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent pushing﴾ [al-Tur: 13], and this has already been discussed. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿That is the one who repulses the orphan﴾, that is, he pushes him away from his right. Qatadah said: he oppresses him and wrongs him. The meanings are close. This has already been discussed in Surat al-Nisa', that they did not give inheritance to women or to children, and they would say: "Only one who thrusts with the spear and strikes with the sword inherits the wealth." It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever takes in an orphan among the Muslims until he becomes self-sufficient, Paradise is certainly due to him." This meaning has passed in more than one place.

The second: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾, that is, he does not command it, out of his stinginess and his denial of the requital. It is like His saying, exalted is He, in Surat al-Haqqah: ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾ [al-Haqqah: 34], and this has already been discussed. The blame is not general so as to include one who leaves it out due to inability; rather, they used to be stingy and make excuses for themselves, saying: ﴿Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 47]. So this verse was revealed concerning them, and the blame was directed at them. The meaning of the sentence is: they do not do it when they are able, and they do not urge others to do it when they are in hardship.

The third: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So woe to those who pray﴾, that is, a punishment for them. This has been discussed in more than one place.

﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: it is the one who prays, but if he prays he does not hope for reward for it, and if he abandons it he does not fear punishment for it. Also from him: those who delay it beyond its times. Likewise al-Mughirah related from Ibrahim, who said: "heedless" means wasting the time. From Abu al-ʿAliyah: they do not pray it at its appointed times, nor do they complete its bowing or prostration. I say: this is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer﴾ [Maryam: 59], as its explanation has passed in Surat Maryam, peace be upon her. It is also related from Ibrahim: that it is one who, when he prostrates, raises his head turning to the side like this. Qutrub said: it is that he does not recite nor remember Allah. In the reading of ʿAbdullah it is "alladhina hum ʿan salatihim lahun" (who are heedless of their prayer). Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas said: the Prophet ﷺ said concerning His saying, "So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer," and he said: "Those who delay the prayer beyond its time, out of neglect towards it." Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: what is the difference between His saying "ʿan salatihim" and your saying "fi salatihim"? I say: the meaning of "ʿan" is that they are heedless of it with the heedlessness of abandoning it and paying it little attention, and that is the act of the hypocrites, or of the wicked rogues among the Muslims. The meaning of "fi" is that heedlessness overtakes them within it, through the whispering of a devil or a passing thought of the self, and this hardly any Muslim is free from. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself would experience heedlessness in his prayer, let alone others, and for this reason the jurists included the chapter on the prostration of forgetfulness in their books. Everyone who never forgets in his prayer is a man who does not reflect upon it, nor understand its recitation; his concern is with its counts, and this is a man who eats the husks and throws away the kernel. The Prophet ﷺ only forgot in his prayer because of his thought on something greater than it. Except that one who turns towards the whisperings of Satan may forget in his prayer, when he is told: "Remember this, remember that," what he was not remembering, until a man does not know how many he has prayed.

The reality of showing off is seeking worldly gain through worship, and its root is seeking status in people's hearts. Its first form is beautifying one's bearing, which is one of the parts of prophethood, and by it he intends rank and praise. The second: showing off through short or rough garments, to take on the appearance of asceticism in the world. The third: showing off through speech, by displaying disgust at the people of the world, and displaying admonition and regret over the good and obedience that escapes one. The fourth: showing off by displaying prayer and charity, or by beautifying the prayer for the sake of people seeing it; and this is lengthy, and this is its indication; this was said by Ibn al-ʿArabi. I say: the discussion on showing off, its rulings and its reality has already been discussed in Surat al-Nisa', Hud and the end of al-Kahf, sufficiently. And praise be to Allah.

The fifth: A person is not a show-off by displaying an act of righteousness if it is an obligatory act, for it is the right of obligatory acts to be announced and made known, due to his saying, peace be upon him: "And there is no concealing of the obligations of Allah" [i.e., they are not hidden nor concealed, but manifested, announced and openly done], because they are the signs of Islam and the symbols of the religion, and because one who abandons them deserves blame and hatred, so it is obligatory to remove suspicion by making them apparent. If it is a voluntary act, its right is to be concealed, because one is not blamed for leaving it and there is no suspicion in it; but if he displays it intending to be followed in it, it is good. Showing off is only that one intends by displaying it that eyes should see him, so that he is praised for righteousness. It was related from one of them that he saw a man in the mosque who had performed a prostration of thanks and lengthened it, and he said: "How good this would be if it were in your house." He only said this because he perceived in him showing off and seeking reputation. This meaning has passed in Surat al-Baqarah at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you disclose your charities﴾ [al-Baqarah: 271], and in other places. And praise be to Allah for that.

The sixth: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and withhold small kindnesses﴾. Concerning it there are twelve opinions.

The first: that it is the zakat of their wealth. Thus al-Dahhak related from Ibn ʿAbbas. Something similar was related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, and this was said by Malik. What is meant by it is the hypocrite who withholds it. Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related from Malik, who said: It has reached me that the saying of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who make show of their deeds, and withhold small kindnesses﴾, means that the hypocrite, when he prays, prays for show, and if it escapes him he does not regret it; and "withhold small kindnesses" means the zakat which Allah made obligatory upon them. Zayd ibn Aslam said: if prayer were hidden from them as zakat was hidden from them, they would not pray.

The second opinion: that al-Ma'un is wealth, in the language of Quraysh; this was said by Ibn Shihab and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab.

A third opinion: that it is a comprehensive term for the benefits of the household, such as the axe, the cooking pot, fire and what resembles these; this was said by Ibn Masʿud, and it was also related from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Aʿsha said:

"With one more generous than him with his small kindnesses, when their sky does not rain."

The fourth: al-Zajjaj, Abu ʿUbayd and al-Mubarrad mentioned that al-Ma'un in the Jahiliyyah was everything that has benefit in it, even the axe, the pot, the bucket and the flint, and everything that has benefit, whether little or much; and they recited the verse of al-Aʿsha. They said: and al-Ma'un in Islam is obedience and zakat, and they recited the saying of al-Ra'i:

Arabs, who see that from our wealth the right of zakat is sent down as a sending down,
A people upon Islam who have not withheld their small kindnesses, nor neglected the tahlil."

The fifth: that it is lending, related from Ibn ʿAbbas as well. The sixth: that it is all good conduct which people practise among themselves; this was said by Muhammad ibn Kaʿb and al-Kalbi. Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 107, verse 1–7 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Whom you encounter [strike] in the battle...﴾ [[In the tafsir of al-Tha'labi: "Whom you strive against (tujahiduhunna)", which is the more apt reading.]] ... ﴿in fetters﴾ ... ﴿they submit or give﴾ ... ﴿with ma'un [small kindnesses]﴾ [[al-Biran (with the ba' vowelled either as a damma or a kasra): plural of birrah, which here means the ring in a camel's nose. It also means any ring of a bracelet, earring or anklet.]]

It has also been said: it is what it is not permissible to withhold, such as water, salt and fire, because 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the thing that it is not permissible to withhold?" He said: [Water, fire and salt.] I said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is water, but what about fire and salt?" He said: [O 'A'ishah, whoever gives fire, it is as if he has given in charity everything that is cooked with that fire, and whoever gives salt, it is as if he has given in charity everything that is seasoned with that salt, and whoever gives a drink of water where water is found, it is as if he has freed sixty souls, and whoever gives a drink of water where it is not found, it is as if he has given life to a soul, and whoever gives it life, it is as if he has given life to all of mankind.] This was mentioned by al-Tha'labi in his tafsir, and Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan. In its chain there is weakness (lin), and this is the twelfth opinion.

Al-Mawardi: It is possible that it means the lending of things whose use is light, and Allah has made it heavy [i.e., blameworthy].

And Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn 'Abbas, was asked: "Whoever withholds some goods, will he have woe?" He said: "No, but whoever combines all three, for him is woe," meaning: neglecting the prayer, showing off, and stinginess with ma'un.

I say: It is more fitting that these attributes apply to the hypocrites, and they are more deserving of them, since they combined the three attributes: neglecting the prayer, showing off, and stinginess with wealth. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people, and they do not remember Allah except a little﴾ [[Verse 142, Surah an-Nisa'.]] [an-Nisa': 142], and He said: ﴿And they do not spend except while they are unwilling﴾ [[Verse 54, Surah at-Tawbah.]] [at-Tawbah: 54]. These are their states, and it is far-fetched that they be found in a sincere believing Muslim. If some of them are found in him, a part of the rebuke reaches him, and that is in withholding ma'un when it is required, as in prayer when he abandons it. And Allah knows best. It is only a base refusal in terms of manliness outside of cases of necessity. And Allah knows best.
